title: The Peak of Every Kind
content_summary: Cover slide with the deck title and subtitle over a graph-paper background.
text_blocks: Al-Naysaburi's Natural Witness to the Imamate

title: The Architecture of a Domain
content_summary: A hub-and-spoke diagram showing a central summit radiating to five ranked members of a domain.
text_blocks: A domain is crowned not by the member most acted upon, but by the one that originates and quickens.

Among the four physical elements, fire alone is placed at the summit. While cold and dryness receive and take on qualities, fire acts. It illumines, elevates, and stirs the inert into life. The summit is always the giver.

title: The Grand Catalogue of Peaks
content_summary: A four-column table mapping each material domain to its specimen, hidden criterion, and spiritual proof.
text_blocks: The highest religious pillar giving light to souls.
The sun of religion through whom insight shines.
The intellectual substance settling the dealings of creation.
The peak from whom souls draw livelihood and knowledge.
Total Utility (mirrors the human, nothing wasted)
The ultimate figure of benefit received.

title: The Ruby's Criterion
content_summary: A central ruby withstanding fire and flood, contrasted with three lesser gems that alter under pressure.
text_blocks: The Red Ruby: Purity, radiance, and weight remain entirely unchanged. The natural proxy for an authority that cannot be corrupted.
Prized, yet vulnerable to alteration under pressure.

title: The Divergence of Medicine
content_summary: A two-column contrast between the True Imam as antidote and the Usurper as poison.
text_blocks: Revelation as cure. Rescues souls dying of doubt when mild remedies fail.
Fatal poisons and worthless stones. Counterfeits that destroy the souls of those who trust them.

title: The Sensory Sorting of Guides
content_summary: A three-column table sorting guides by sensory trait, spiritual output, and archetype.
text_blocks: The True Imams (Deep roots, endless fruit)
Gives neither food nor delight; sickens
Imams of Error (Uprooted tree, no footing)
The Literalists (Ahl al-Zahir, clinging only to the outer husk)

title: The Escalation of the Animal Kingdom
content_summary: A three-step ascending flow from mastery to generosity to organized leadership under the lead bee.
text_blocks: The Escalation of the Animal Kingdom
1. Mastery: Horse, Eagle, Lion. Excellence achieved via physical dominance, speed, or mastery of the hunt.
2. Generosity: Gazelle, Bee. Excellence refined via yielding a precious product the world could not otherwise have (musk, honey).
3. Organized Leadership: The Ya'sub (Lead Bee). The ultimate natural image: a community ordered entirely around its Chief to produce a cure for mankind.

title: The Human Paradox
content_summary: A flow diagram showing plants, metals, and animals feeding into Human Reason, which processes and steers them.
text_blocks: The Trap: Man redirects nature, but this mastery is an engine that must be steered.
The Processor: Reason. Without the human capacity to extract, crossbreed, and cultivate, the latent excellence of the cosmos remains invisible.
System Input: The merits of the whole world are gathered and enfolded into the human frame.

title: The Ultimate Ruin vs. The Ultimate Summit
content_summary: A diverging line chart from Human Reason: one path rises to the Imam-governed summit, the other plummets below the Baseline of Beasts.
text_blocks: The Ultimate Ruin vs. The Ultimate Summit
Governed by the Imam: Reason steered by the summit. Virtues acquired, latent excellence unlocked, creation justified.
Ungoverned Reason: Refusing the guide turns the mastery of reason into an instrument of profound corruption. Plummets below the beast, which only acts on use and does not scheme its own ruin.

title: The Teleological Loop
content_summary: A circular flow linking Nature, Humanity, the Imam, and the Creator, with a synthesis and conclusion panel.
text_blocks: Justifies and fulfills the wisdom of...
The catalogue was never merely about nature. It is a structural proof that without the Imam, human excellence remains hidden. Without human excellence, nature's worth is never known.
The natural order terminates not in an abstraction, but in an absolute obligation: to receive religion from the guides for whose sake the cosmos was made.
